newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call rates easy on low demand, gilts active.
newsitem.headline: Indian call rates easy on low demand, gilts active.

text.p: Indian call money rates ended easy at 0.25-0.50 percent on Tuesday, against the day's opening levels of 0.50-1.00 percent, dealers said.
"Absolutely dull, no demand for funds, most of the borrowers have covered for reporting Friday," a dealer with private bank said.
Call rates declined in staggered steps from opening quotes of 1.0 percent to 0.25 percent towards the close, he said.
There was a great demand for short-dated and medium term securities and treasury bills.

Excess money refunds from a recent oversubscribed state government bond auction and from a State Industrial Development Bank Of India (SIDBI) primary issue, fed demand for securites, said Felix D'cunna, vice president, at Tower Capital Investment
D'cunna said bankers with covered positions and receiving a sudden inflow of funds rushed to invest in short to medium term government paper.
Volume rose to 4.80 billion rupees, against the previous days 4.43 billion rupees, he said.

The securities prices rose by 5-10 basis points across the maturity, with 13.50 percent 1997 stock up ten basis points at 102.95 rupees and 13.40 percent 1999 stock up eight basis points at 101.27 rupees, dealers said.
The yield treasury bills maturing in January 1997, fell by 15 basis points to 9.85 percent, against it previous close, dealer said.
